findings.title: The Step-0 instrument-equivalence section describes gbg round import <pile> / round compare as built, but the CLI refuses both
locations: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1961-1963 — 'Three verbs carry it, and they are defined here'
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1965-1979 — 'gbg round import <pile…> writes into the consumer's .gbg/rounds/<round>/ ... It writes ROUND.toml ..., findings.json ..., import.json'
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1980-1981 — 'gbg round grade <round> ... re-computes the tally from the imported verdict files'
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1982-1999 — 'gbg round compare --recorded <recorded.toml> <round> compares that re-graded tally ... The four count keys are the only ones compared ...'
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:2001-2019 — the per-consumer 'Recorded target' table presented as ported/verified data
findings.description: This section presents `gbg round import <pile…>` and `gbg round compare --recorded` as operative CLI verbs with a precise, detailed contract (ROUND.toml field population from the pile, findings.json built from a title→id map, a four-key comparison with a 0/1/2 exit contract). The actual implementation in src/CLI/Rounds.jl (cmd_round, lines 876-880) explicitly refuses both: a non-`--empty` `round import` prints 'the legacy pile readers are Phase 2's scratch tools (IMPLEMENTATION Phase 2 step 1); only `--empty` exists yet' and returns 2, and `round compare` unconditionally prints 'round compare --recorded: written with Phase 2's scratch imports' and returns 2. Only the degenerate `gbg round import --empty` path (import_empty, Rounds.jl:735-756) exists. The document gives no signal that this is a planned-but-unbuilt feature — it reads as a completed, tested mechanism (down to the exact recorded-target counts per consumer pile), which misleads a reader trying to use ARCHITECTURE.md as ground truth for the tool's current behaviour (RULE.DOC.CURRENT).
findings.resolution_hint: Mark the whole Step-0 subsection as a planned design (e.g. a leading 'Not yet built (IMPLEMENTATION Phase 2 step 1):' clause, matching the phrasing the CLI itself already uses), or move it to a forward-looking roadmap section, until the pile importer and `round compare` actually exist.

findings.title: gbg round import is claimed to need no .gbg/config.toml and to run self verify first, but cmd_round requires the config unconditionally and import_empty never calls self_verify
locations: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1975-1976 — 'It needs no `.gbg/config.toml` — the one `round` verb that runs before `init`; `self verify` still precedes it'
findings.description: cmd_round (src/CLI/Rounds.jl:855) calls `cfg = Config.read()` unconditionally before dispatching to any round verb, including import; Config.read() (src/CLI/Config.jl:257-261) throws a ConfigError when `.gbg/config.toml` does not exist. That error is not caught by cmd_round's own try/catch (which only catches RoundError) and instead surfaces at Main.jl's top-level handler (Main.jl:144-150) as an exit-3 crash — not the config-free success the text describes. Separately, the one import path that IS implemented, import_empty (Rounds.jl:735-756), never calls guard()/self_verify() at all, unlike every other round verb (prepare, build, test, bank, rerun, abandon all call guard(), which runs self_verify — Rounds.jl:66,147,295,313,469,701,830), so 'self verify still precedes it' does not hold for the code as written.
findings.resolution_hint: Either special-case `gbg round import` (both variants) in cmd_round to skip Config.read() before init, or correct the prose to state that `.gbg/config.toml` is in fact required and that self-verify is not run before import.

findings.title: Historical measurement lines (e.g. SCAN.ID_RESOLVES's 964/11, SIGNATURE_MIRROR's 247/251) are stated as bare current-reading facts with no reproducible current-tree pointer
locations: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:2455 — 'Measured before it was built: 964 references here, 11 unresolved, all 11 artefacts of the pattern'
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:2362 — 'Narrowed to `names` 2026-09-12, the form 247 of 251 docstrings here already took'
findings.description: Both counts are historical point-in-time measurements folded into otherwise-present-tense rule/scan descriptions, with no note of how a reader would reproduce or re-check them today (a live run of SCAN.ID_RESOLVES against the current tree returns 0 hits, which is consistent but not obviously so without re-running it; docstring_blocks() over src+ext currently returns 298 total blocks, a different and not directly comparable denominator to the claimed 251). This is a self-containment/verifiability gap rather than an outright falsehood — RULE.DOC.SELF_CONTAINED asks that a rationale document read complete without depending on unstated context, and 'here' in both sentences is ambiguous between 'at measurement time' and 'now'.
findings.resolution_hint: Date-stamp both counts explicitly (e.g. 'measured 2026-09-12') so they read unambiguously as historical snapshots rather than current live counts, consistent with how nearby Revision-history entries already date their measurements.
